slides.title: Palantir has a real but temporary advantage, and it hinges on keeping its deployment method in-house
slides.subtitle: Theory of value: Palantir sustains value-creating growth by owning the ontology and operational-integration layer, proven in national security, and combining it with forward-deployed engineering and AIP, so that AI is embedded in each customer's live workflows.
slides.meta: Define → Create → Capture → Deliver · evidence labelled V = verified, A = assumed

slides.title: Palantir sells governed AI into the live operations of large institutions; its 'why' leans on a lock-in premise that is unproven

left.heading: Who
left.text: Operations-heavy institutions: US/allied defense and intelligence, plus large operators in manufacturing, energy, health and supply chain. ~220 deals of $1M+ per quarter (V).

left.heading: What
left.text: Governed AI in live workflows in weeks, via ontology + AIP (permissions, lineage, action write-back). 'Weeks vs years' is company-claimed (A).

left.heading: Why
left.text: Trust, forward-deployed engineers and an embedded ontology are meant to raise switching costs and drive expansion. Exit-cost effect unproven (A).

right.heading: The Define argument
lines: P1  Operations-heavy institutions need AI that changes live decisions, because spend keeps deepening (US commercial +149%, V; NDR 157%, CFO-stated, unfiled).
P2  Palantir delivers it faster than self-build or bare model APIs, because the ontology supplies what they lack (A).
P3  Palantir keeps the value, because each workflow raises exit cost (P3a, A) and rivals lack parity for ~3 years (A).
C   Palantir creates and captures value for roughly 2–3 years; longer only if P3a is shown.

right.heading: Segway test: passes, conditional on P3a
right.text: WHO is still wide in commercial; contracts allow termination for convenience (V, 10-Q), which cuts against lock-in.

slides.source: Sources: Palantir Q2 2026 8-K Ex. 99.1 and 10-Q (SEC EDGAR); NDR from the CFO's prepared remarks on the earnings call (not in filings).

slides.title: Palantir wins on willingness to pay, not on cost, but the size of its WTP gap over an SI-led build is unmeasured

left.heading: Position statement
left.text: For operations-heavy institutions that need AI to change live decisions, Palantir offers governed AI deployed into their workflows, better than an SI-led build on Databricks or a hyperscaler stack, because ontology, forward deployment, AIP and accredited trust work as one system.

left.heading: Side: higher WTP
left.text: Cost is not the claim. The 85% gross margin reflects software mix, and FDE cost sits partly in S&M (V, 10-Q). Evidence shows only WTP ≥ price; no commercial win/loss data exists.

left.heading: Cost / quality frontier
left.text: High-quality, high-cost end: defensible but thin. Neighbours are Anduril (government) and AI-lab ventures (commercial); Databricks, Fabric and AWS crowd the low-cost end.

right.title: Value stick per top account (index, WTP = top of bar)
right.note: ILLUSTRATIVE (A): WTP 100 vs 70, price 40 vs 20, cost 15 vs 14. No measured rival WTP.

slides.source: Sources: Palantir Q2 2026 10-Q (gross margin, cost classification); value sticks are assumed.

slides.title: The edge is a capability system on a clock of about two years, and inimitability is its weakest link

left.heading: Weakest letter: I on the ontology
left.text: OSDK openness plus copying by AI labs and data platforms. Four interlocking parts copied at 90% fidelity each yield 0.9⁴ ≈ 66% (A).

left.heading: Barber test: tried, not yet failed
left.text: OpenAI's Deployment Company (>$4B, ~150 FDEs; V) and Anthropic's services JV (~$1.5B; V, secondary) are both copying forward deployment.

right.heading: Advantage type
right.text: Capability-based (the system), with a thin positional layer (accreditations).

right.heading: Durability
right.text: Temporary: ~2 yrs in top commercial accounts, 1–2 yrs mid-size, 2–3 yrs government (A, judgement).

right.heading: Scalability
right.text: Scales in depth (top accounts), not breadth; capped by FDE supply and AIP substitution.

slides.source: Sources: OpenAI Deployment Company announcement (search excerpt); Fortune citing WSJ on the Anthropic JV. Clocks are judgement.

slides.title: Substitutes cap industry profit: in commercial, the option to build it yourself sets the price ceiling

rows: Few accredited players, and the Army buys two; in commercial, Databricks, Snowflake, Fabric and the AI labs
Accreditation takes years; commercial entry needs only capital and distribution
Monopsony buyer, volume tiers, termination rights; commercial buyers hold the build option
Clouds and model providers are also rivals; scarce FDE talent is paid in SBC
SI-led builds and near-zero-price bundles from platforms

right.heading: Most threatening force
right.text: The build option caps price, and buyer power works through it.

right.heading: Industry boundary
right.text: Two industries share one product: government (US/allied) and commercial operational-AI platforms. Revenue split ≈ 51 / 49 (V, 10-Q).

slides.source: Sources: Palantir Q2 2026 10-Q (segment revenue); Army enterprise agreements (Washington Technology, DefenseScoop).

slides.title: Palantir out-earns peers with different business models, but its margin lead is growth leverage, not proven pricing power

left.title: Operating margin tracks growth (%)
left.note: Gross margin held at 79–85% across 17–93% growth: software-normal, not a premium. FY23/24 10-Ks, FY25 secondary, Q2'26 8-K (V).

right.text: *Unresolved: 10-K reading ~13.7% at ~19% growth. Either figure beats Palantir's 5–11% at similar growth.

right.heading: Pushes back on: substitutes
right.text: Write-back workflows raise the cost of moving to a build (A). Price per workflow at renewal is not observed.

right.heading: Consistent with Create? Only weakly
right.text: Shows WTP ≥ price, not a WTP premium. Value may leak to buyers (EA volume tiers) and employees (SBC +66% y/y).

slides.source: Sources: Palantir 10-Ks FY23/FY24, Q2 2026 8-K and 10-Q; peer margins via search summaries.

slides.title: The system half of the advantage is well organized: product, in-house FDEs and bootcamps reinforce each other

full.heading: Create source, restated
full.text: The ontology/AIP system, plus a tacit deployment method and accredited trust, which together put governed AI into live workflows in weeks.

rows: Each workflow adds objects and write-back
Carry the method; demand outruns capacity
Loosen capacity; risk diffusing the method
A capture leak, not a source issue
Retention tied to the share price

slides.source: Sources: Palantir Q2 2026 10-Q (cash, SBC); Accenture newsroom (Dec 2025); Fujitsu FDE partner announcement (Sep 2026).

slides.title: The method half is exposed: partner scale-up and pay tied to the share price could leak what rivals cannot yet copy

left.heading: Misfit 1 · Unlimited partner scope
left.text: Partners that also serve Databricks diffuse the method (hits VRIO 'I'). Accenture's Palantir group has 2,000+ staff (V).
bullets: Fix: partners deliver scoped work only; tie volume to not dual-sourcing.

left.heading: Misfit 2 · SBC-only retention
left.text: Method carriers can leave for AI-lab deployment arms if the stock falls. SBC $265M in Q2, +66% y/y (V, 10-Q).
bullets: Fix: targeted cash retention from the $9.4B cash pile (cost A).

right.heading: Fix that matters most
right.text: Design stays in-house; partners only deliver. Palantir controls the lever, and it is the stage's breaking premise. Cost: slower growth than demand allows.

right.heading: Link to VRIO 'O' · Verdict: partly organized
right.text: Yes on the system, unproven on the method.

right.heading: Unresolved
right.text: Who designs the ontology in partner deployments? Partner literature says SIs do (secondary).

slides.source: Sources: Accenture newsroom; Palantir Q2 2026 10-Q; partner articles (secondary).

slides.title: A real but temporary advantage: durability depends on one assumed premise, that the deployment method stays in-house

left.heading: The full argument
lines: P1  Operations-heavy institutions need AI that changes live decisions, because spend is deepening (US commercial +149%, V).
P2  Palantir creates more value than an SI build, because its ontology/AIP system plus tacit method delivers governed action faster (WTP ≥ price shown; premium not).
P3  It keeps software-normal gross margin plus a growth-dependent operating premium, because it holds off substitutes in top accounts only.
P4  It is partly organized: the system fits; the method is exposed through partners and SBC.
C   Capability-based, temporary advantage (~2 yrs commercial, 2–3 yrs government) that depends on keeping the method in-house.

right.heading: Cross-stage findings
bullets: Define's WHY (lock-in) is stronger than Create supports (temporary scarcity).
Capture shows WTP ≥ price, not a WTP premium.
Deliver straddles: scales via partners while claiming the method is tacit.

right.heading: Weakest premise
right.text: Scoping and ontology design stay with Palantir-controlled people. Settle it with partner SOWs and NDR for partner-led vs FDE-led cohorts.

right.heading: Implication (no decision was posed)
right.text: Prioritize scope control and price-independent retention. Tripwires: gross margin <78% for 2 qtrs; NDR <130%; growth <30% with op. margin <15%.
